candidates.source_title: How a Shaved Head Becomes a Powdered Wig 🪒
candidates.source_description:
You shave your head to beat lice... so you build a powdered wig, one problem at a time. A poor girl's hair sewn on a cap, clay pipe curlers baked in a pie, animal fat, scented flour, a leather cone over your face, a silk bag and a powder tax.
Based on the real periwigs of the 1660s on: Samuel Pepys had his hair cut off for a £3 wig in 1663 and sent one back "full of nits" in 1667; wigmakers baked the curls in dough in a baker's oven; Britain taxed hair powder at one guinea a year from 1795; judg
